reviewed_arguments: Graded source and target component degrees remain literal. Finite-dimensional homogeneous normalization is not substituted by an unproved actual order reducer. All real mapping exponents follow from the exact entry orders.

Full rectangular quantization uses the actual frame and density factors. Existing K1a is adapted to finitely many global chart/entry families, and every classical remainder of the asymptotic sum is proved from its finite initial segments.
The actual C_N has only the proved weighted order-minus-one projection defect. Its full original measurements and stable principal bundle are retained.

Onto and injective hypotheses are distinguished. Both rectangular Gram inverses are positive, smooth and uniformly controlled on compact normalized sets, without assuming the stable projection is orthogonal.

The right construction uses B C_N squared and literal finite right corrections T0 sum E^l. The left column (B,I-C_N) uses literal left corrections sum F^l L0. The complete asymptotic sums give their two separate smooth errors.
S=C_N T has an order-one range error and B S-I has an order-one error; only B C_N S-I is proved smoothing. All these identities retain the exact original factors and signs.

Bijectivity identifies the leading symbols of T-prime and S, giving only their order-one difference. Exact R0 and R1 reconstruction preserves both the negative sign in S-double-prime C_N and the full C_N squared defect.

Every original entry degree and all-real Sobolev map is restored directly. Both the one-step reconstruction estimate and the stronger smoothing-row estimate begin with distributions of a known lower level, avoiding a circular trace claim.
Zero-dimensional compact boundaries, empty cospheres, zero-rank fibers and empty manifolds retain their exact finite-dimensional remainder identities.

The four complete calculations prove sharp surviving errors on circle modes, nonorthogonal right/left factors, independent rank hypotheses and the original high/fractional boundary weights. The existing periodization proof is explicitly adapted to every displayed multiplier.
